High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Amit Dave - Advocate for the petitioners.

Shri Tapan Bathre - Panel Lawyer for respondents No.1 t
Heard on admission.
By the instant petition, the petitioners are challenging the prosecution initiated beyond the period of limitation prescribed under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
As per the said provision, the maximum period for initiation of prosecution is three years that too with the sanction of the Commissioner.
In normal course, it has to be filed within a period of one year from the date of commission of offence.

However, in the complaint, it is mentioned that the date of commission of offence was 14.03.2012 and complaint was filed on 20.02.2015 i.e. beyond the period of one year,
although within the period of three years as per the proviso.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is no sanction of Commissioner and as such the respondents cannot take initiate prosecution in the absence of sanction by the Commissioner beyond the period of three years as per the aforesaid provision.
Let notice be issued to the respondents on payment of process fee within seven days by RAD mode,
returnable within four weeks.

As an interim measure, it is directed that no further proceeding pursuant to the Complaint Case - RCT No.947/2015 pending in the Court of 2 MCRC-15625-2025 JMFC, Bhopal shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Sudesh Liyaqat Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108685760/
